llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and install requirements are consistent with a Shanghai Library seat-booking CLI that reads/writes local profile auth files and optionally uses Playwright for browser-assisted login.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the code and files: scripts call the yuyue.library.sh.cn APIs to list/availability/book/cancel seats and manage local profile auth files. Required binaries (node/npm/npx) and Playwright dependency are appropriate for a Node.js + browser-automation implementation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts limit runtime actions to: opening a browser for manual login (Playwright), reading/writing profile JSON files under ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking, and making HTTPS requests to the library API host. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files, environment secrets, or to send data to third-party endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata includes a brew entry to install Node on macOS; the project itself depends on Playwright (in package.json) and SKILL.md instructs npm/npx to install Playwright and its browsers. This is normal but the install metadata does not enumerate npm/browser installs explicitly — users should be aware Playwright will download browser binaries when installed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are requested. The skill legitimately reads and writes local profile auth files (accessToken, sign, timestamp, optional xEncode) in ~/.config/shlibrary-seat-booking/profiles or a user-specified auth-file; this is proportionate to its purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request permanent/always-enabled privileges. It writes only to its own profile directory (config path documented) and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This repository appears to implement exactly what it claims: a Node.js CLI that uses Playwright to help extract library auth headers and then calls the library's reservation APIs. Before installing/running: 1) review the login.js script if you are uncomfortable with browser automation; it will open a browser and capture auth headers after you manually log in. 2) Protect the generated profile files (they contain accessToken/sign/timestamp) — keep them in a secure location and follow the README suggestion (chmod 600). 3) Installing Playwright will download browser binaries; do this in an environment you control. 4) Confirm you trust the GitHub source (homepage) before running code that will execute locally. If you want extra assurance, run the code in an isolated environment (container or VM) the first time.
